steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Prosocial behaviour is any act that benefits others. Altruism is helping with no expectation of personal gain - the debate is whether true altruism exists or whether all helping is ultimately self-serving. | Key Fact: The bystander effect: people are less likely to help when others are present. Latane & Darley's (1968) smoke experiment: 75% helped when alone vs 10-38% when in a group. | Key Fact: Diffusion of responsibility: in a group, each person assumes someone else will help. This was famously linked to the murder of Kitty Genovese (1964), where 38 witnesses allegedly did nothing - though later accounts question this version. | Key Fact: The cost-reward model (Piliavin): people weigh up the costs of helping against the rewards.
